source_key_points: 6 CONSTRUCTIONS AND TILINGS 6.1 Geometric Constructions Eyes Do you recall the ‘Eyes’ construction we did in Grade 6?
Of course, eyes can be drawn freehand, but we wanted to construct them so that the lower arc and upper arc of each eye look symmetrical.
We relied on our spatial estimation to determine the two centres, A and B (see the figure), from which we drew A the lower arc and upper arc respectively.
The arcs define a line XY that ‘supports’ the drawing though it is not part of the final figure.
We can start with this supporting line and systematically find the centres A and B.
For the eye to be symmetrical, or for the X Y supporting line to be the line of symmetry, the upper and lower arcs should have the same radius.
Since AX = AY and BX = BY, this means B AX = AY = BX = BY Chapter-6.indd 136 10/17/2025 3:19:36 PM Constructions and Tilings How do we find such A and B?
A From X and Y, draw arcs above and below XY, with the same radii.
The two points at which the arcs meet, X Y above and below XY, give us A and B, respectively.

content.overview: In this chapter, we explore the fascinating world of geometric constructions and tilings. Constructions involve creating geometric figures using only a compass and straightedge. Tilings are patterns formed by covering a plane using specific geometric shapes (like triangles, squares, and hexagons) without any gaps or overlaps. This chapter lays the foundation for understanding how shapes fit together in space.

teacher_explanation.subject: Mathematics
teacher_explanation.content: This chapter introduces students to geometric constructions and tilings. It covers fundamental techniques for drawing geometric shapes on paper using only a compass and straightedge, such as drawing perpendicular bisectors, constructing specific polygons, and finding intersections of lines. It also introduces the concept of tessellations, which are patterns of shapes that fill a plane without gaps. The chapter includes various types of tessellations, including regular, irregular, and semi-regular tilings, and explores the properties related to symmetry and angle sums. The chapter aims to develop spatial reasoning, precision in drawing, and an understanding of how geometric figures interact in a two-dimensional space.

story_mode.subject: Mathematics
story_mode.content: Imagine a master architect tasked with designing a decorative pattern for a temple floor. The architect must use precise mathematical techniques (constructions) to draw the boundary of the temple and then use specific shapes (tilings) to fill the floor completely, ensuring no stones are left out and no stones overlap. The story of this chapter is one of transformation: starting with simple tools (compass and straightedge) and applying logical rules to create infinite, beautiful geometric patterns. We will see how a single triangle or square can generate a complex, repeating design, showcasing the power of symmetry and tessellation.

chapter_summary.subject: Mathematics
chapter_summary.content: Chapter 206, 'Constructions and Tilings,' serves as a practical guide to the intersection of geometry and design. It provides the essential tools for creating precise geometric figures and an understanding of how regular polygons can perfectly tile a plane. Key themes include the use of the compass and straightedge, the concept of tessellation (tiling), and the importance of symmetry in geometric patterns. By mastering these concepts, students gain a foundational skill in spatial reasoning, pattern recognition, and a deep appreciation for the mathematical structures that govern the visible world.
